hypothesis: x86_64 PGO was blocked by rustc's LLVM crashing while instrumenting the reth crate (SIGILL in libLLVM.so.23.1-rust-1.99.1 on stable). Nightly carries a different LLVM build, so the same two-pass PGO may simply compile. Worth one attempt because m8azn-3xl is the fastest box measured (4.51s) and PGO is worth -6% on ARM; nightly also brings evm2's tail-call dispatch, which was neutral on ARM, so a win here is attributable to PGO.
llm_commentary: x86_64 PGO is unblocked by a nightly toolchain, and it is the largest PGO gain measured: i7i 6.38s [6.43/6.38/6.34] → 5.59s [5.59/5.58/5.59], -12.4% with disjoint ranges and a remarkably tight spread (0.01s). The blocker was specific to stable rustc 1.99.1's LLVM 23.1, which died with SIGILL inside libLLVM while instrumenting the reth crate; nightly 1.101.0 (LLVM from 2026-11-04) compiles the same instrumented build without complaint, so this was a toolchain bug rather than anything about reth or the flags. Note the run bundles nightly's evm2 tail-call dispatch with PGO+THP, but tail-call dispatch measured neutral-to-harmful on ARM once PGO was applied (4.36 vs 4.31), so the gain here is almost certainly PGO+THP rather than dispatch. Full stack on i7i: 8.09 → 6.38 (code) → 5.59 (PGO+THP) = -30.9%.
